newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-UEFA CALL HEARING ON WEAH-COSTA INCIDENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA CALL HEARING ON WEAH-COSTA INCIDENT.

text.p: UEFA said on Friday it had called a special disciplinary hearing next week on the scuffle involving AC Milan's George Weah after Wednesday's Champions' League match.
Porto defender Jorge Costa suffered a broken nose in the incident which took place in the player's tunnel at the end of an ill-tempered match.
The 30-year-old Weah, hailed by FIFA as a model of fair play, could face a lengthy suspension if European soccer's governing body found he had attacked Costa in the post-match clash.
Costa could also face sanctions if UEFA found he had provoked the incident with racist taunts.
UEFA spokesman Rene Eberle said the disciplinary hearing would be held next week but would not say on which day or where it would take place.

"The decision will probably be made at the latter end of next week," he said. "It all depends on the reports and the eye-witnesses. We may well have to call our own investigation and decide later on."
Costa on Thursday needed surgery after breaking his nose in the incident, witnessed by a UEFA official following a tense 1-1 Group D draw littered with fouls and yellow cards.
Porto club doctor Jose Carlos Esteves said Weah had head-butted Costa.
Milan officials and Weah's wife Claire were quoted as saying the Liberian, holder of the prestigious Golden Ball award to Europe's top player, had reacted to racist taunts.
"That player covered George with spit and insults. Do you know what he was doing? He was baring his teeth and jumping up and down like a monkey," Gazzetta dello Sport quoted Claire Weah as saying.

Milan's managing director Adriano Galliani told the newspaper: "Without accusing anyone, I would just observe that certain things, like spit and racist grunts, are less evident than blood. We will be presenting our version of the facts."
Costa was shown after the incident on Portuguese television with blood streaming from his nose. He is expected to be out of soccer for three weeks.
Milan still need a point from their final Group D match against Norway's Rosenborg Trondheim to be assured of reaching the quarter-finals of a competition they have won five times.
Wednesday's draw meant that Porto, unbeaten so far in the competition and with one Champions' League game to come, finished first in the group and meet the runners-up of Group C in the last eight.
